hook.hook: Nobody tells you November is still garlic planting time

captions.instagram:
Nobody tells you November is still garlic planting time

I break up garlic bulbs just before planting the largest outer cloves from October to November. If you want to know how to grow garlic in the UK, put them in full sun and keep the bed weed-free. Dry the harvested bulbs for 2 to 3 weeks and softneck types can keep for 6 to 9 months.

Check your local frost dates.

hook.hook: Nobody tells you elephant garlic is this easy

captions.instagram:
Nobody tells you elephant garlic is this easy

If you want to learn how to grow elephant garlic in the UK, keep your bed clear because garlic competes poorly with weeds. Plant individual cloves 5–8 cm deep in a sunny spot with well-drained soil. Ease the bulbs out with a fork in July or August so you do not damage your crop.

Check your local frost dates.

4 easy ways to keep fresh spinach before it turns slimy

Fresh spinach goes slimy quickly if left loose in the fridge. Knowing how to store spinach properly stops your harvest going to waste. Wrap unwashed leaves in damp paper in a bag for 5 to 7 days, or blanch for 2 minutes and freeze for up to 12 months.

Check your local frost dates.

If you want to learn how to grow radishes UK style, start by sowing seeds thinly in shallow drills 1 cm deep. Water them regularly in dry weather so the roots stay sweet and do not split. If you end up with more than you can eat, remove the leaves and keep the roots in water in the fridge.

Check your local frost dates.

If you are wondering what to do with too many spring onions, do not let them get tough and strong in the ground. I pull mine when they are pencil-thick and chop them to freeze in bags for cooked dishes. You can also pickle them whole in a light vinegar brine to keep them for one to two months.

hook.hook: More turnips than you can eat? Don't let them rot

captions.instagram:
More turnips than you can eat? Don't let them rot

If you want to know how to grow turnips UK style, keep them regularly watered so roots stay tender. I thin seedlings to 10 to 15 cm apart and pull baby turnips at golf ball size. You can eat young turnips raw in salads or store maincrop roots in damp sand for 2 to 3 months.

Check your local frost dates.
